title: Ada Lovelace
text: Ada Lovelace was an English mathematician and writer, born in London in 1815. She is known for her work on Charles Babbage's proposed Analytical Engine, and her notes on the machine include what is often described as the first published algorithm intended for a computer.

title: Alan Turing
text: Alan Turing was an English mathematician and computer scientist. He formalised the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine, worked at Bletchley Park on breaking German ciphers during the Second World War, and later worked at the University of Manchester.

title: Marie Curie
text: Marie Curie was a physicist and chemist born in Warsaw who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity in Paris. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences, and with Pierre Curie she discovered polonium and radium.

title: Albert Einstein
text: Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist who developed the theory of relativity. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 for his explanation of the photoelectric effect, and worked in Bern, Zurich and Berlin before moving to Princeton in the United States.

title: Isaac Newton
text: Isaac Newton was an English mathematician and physicist who formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation in the Principia. He was a fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge, and later served as President of the Royal Society in London.

title: Charles Darwin
text: Charles Darwin was an English naturalist known for the theory of evolution by natural selection. His observations during the voyage of HMS Beagle, including those made in the Galapagos Islands, informed his book On the Origin of Species, published in 1859.

title: Nikola Tesla
text: Nikola Tesla was a Serbian-American inventor and engineer best known for his contributions to alternating current electricity systems. He emigrated to the United States in 1884, worked briefly for Thomas Edison, and later partnered with George Westinghouse.

title: Grace Hopper
text: Grace Hopper was an American computer scientist and United States Navy rear admiral. She worked on the Harvard Mark I computer, developed one of the first compilers, and her work on machine-independent programming languages led to COBOL.

title: Rosalind Franklin
text: Rosalind Franklin was an English chemist whose X-ray diffraction images of DNA, taken at King's College London, were critical to understanding its double helix structure. She also did important work on the structure of viruses at Birkbeck College.

title: Galileo Galilei
text: Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer and physicist from Pisa. Using an improved telescope he observed the moons of Jupiter and the phases of Venus, and his support for heliocentrism led to a trial by the Roman Inquisition in 1633.

title: Paris
text: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, located on the Seine. It is home to landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre, one of the most visited museums in the world, and it hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1900, 1924 and 2024.

title: Tokyo
text: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and one of the most populous metropolitan areas in the world. Formerly known as Edo, it became the seat of the Emperor in 1868, and it hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1964 and again in 2021.

title: Seoul
text: Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea, located on the Han River. It has been a major settlement for more than two thousand years, hosted the 1988 Summer Olympic Games, and many large South Korean companies have their headquarters in the city.

title: Cairo
text: Cairo is the capital of Egypt and lies on the Nile. The city is close to the Giza pyramid complex, and Al-Azhar University, founded in the tenth century, is one of the oldest continuously operating universities in the world.

title: Amazon River
text: The Amazon River in South America is the largest river in the world by discharge volume. It flows through Peru, Colombia and Brazil to the Atlantic Ocean, and its basin holds the Amazon rainforest, the largest tropical rainforest on Earth.

title: Mount Everest
text: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level, in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and China. Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and the Sherpa mountaineer Tenzing Norgay made the first confirmed ascent in 1953.

title: Sahara
text: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, covering much of North Africa from the Atlantic Ocean to the Red Sea. Countries including Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Mali and Niger lie partly within it, and it receives very little rainfall.

title: Great Barrier Reef
text: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system in the world, in the Coral Sea off the coast of Queensland, Australia. It was designated a World Heritage Site in 1981 and is threatened by rising ocean temperatures and coral bleaching.

title: Venice
text: Venice is a city in northeastern Italy built on a group of islands in a lagoon of the Adriatic Sea. It was the capital of the Republic of Venice for more than a thousand years, and its canals, including the Grand Canal, are crossed by hundreds of bridges.

title: Kyoto
text: Kyoto is a city on the island of Honshu that served as the capital of Japan for more than a thousand years. It is known for Buddhist temples such as Kinkaku-ji, for Shinto shrines, and for the Kyoto Protocol, a climate agreement adopted there in 1997.

title: United Nations
text: The United Nations is an intergovernmental organization founded in 1945 after the Second World War. Its headquarters are in New York City, and its principal organs include the General Assembly, the Security Council and the International Court of Justice in The Hague.

title: World Health Organization
text: The World Health Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health. It was established in 1948, is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and led the global campaign that eradicated smallpox.

title: CERN
text: CERN is a European research organization that operates the largest particle physics laboratory in the world, near Geneva on the border between France and Switzerland. Its Large Hadron Collider was used to discover the Higgs boson in 2012, and Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web there.

title: NASA
text: NASA is the civil space agency of the United States, established in 1958. It ran the Apollo program, which landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon in 1969, and it operates the Hubble Space Telescope with the European Space Agency.

title: Royal Society
text: The Royal Society is a learned society for science based in London, founded in 1660. Its fellows have included Isaac Newton, Charles Darwin and Ernest Rutherford, and it publishes Philosophical Transactions, one of the oldest scientific journals.

title: International Committee of the Red Cross
text: The International Committee of the Red Cross is a humanitarian organization based in Geneva, founded in 1863 by Henry Dunant and others. It works to protect the victims of armed conflict and has received the Nobel Peace Prize three times.

title: European Union
text: The European Union is a political and economic union of member states in Europe. It grew out of the European Coal and Steel Community and the European Economic Community, its institutions sit mainly in Brussels, Luxembourg and Strasbourg, and many members use the euro.

title: Bauhaus
text: The Bauhaus was a German art school founded by Walter Gropius in Weimar in 1919. It later moved to Dessau and then Berlin, and its approach joining crafts, fine arts and industrial design influenced modern architecture before the school closed in 1933.

title: Olympic Games
text: The modern Olympic Games are an international multi-sport event first held in Athens in 1896, inspired by the ancient games at Olympia. They are organized by the International Olympic Committee, founded by Pierre de Coubertin, and the Summer and Winter Games alternate every two years.

title: FIFA World Cup
text: The FIFA World Cup is an international football competition held every four years among men's national teams. The first tournament took place in Uruguay in 1930, and Brazil has won the competition more times than any other country.

title: Printing press
text: The printing press with movable type was developed in Europe by Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz around 1440. The Gutenberg Bible was one of the first major books printed this way, and the technology spread quickly to cities such as Venice and Paris.

title: Steam engine
text: The steam engine converts heat into mechanical work using steam. Thomas Newcomen built an early engine to pump water from mines in England, and improvements by James Watt, including the separate condenser, made steam power central to the Industrial Revolution.

title: Telephone
text: The telephone converts sound into electrical signals so that people can talk over a distance. Alexander Graham Bell received a United States patent for it in 1876, and Thomas Edison and others later improved its microphone.

title: World Wide Web
text: The World Wide Web is an information system in which documents are linked by hyperlinks and reached over the Internet. Tim Berners-Lee proposed it at CERN in 1989, and the World Wide Web Consortium he founded develops its standards.

title: Transistor
text: The transistor is a semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electrical signals. John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley invented it at Bell Labs in 1947 and shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1956 for the work.

title: Penicillin
text: Penicillin is a group of antibiotics first discovered by Alexander Fleming at St Mary's Hospital in London in 1928. Howard Florey and Ernst Chain later developed it into a medicine at the University of Oxford, and the three shared a Nobel Prize in 1945.

title: Linux
text: Linux is a family of open-source operating systems based on the Linux kernel, first released by Linus Torvalds in 1991 while he was a student at the University of Helsinki. It runs most of the world's servers and supercomputers, and Android is built on it.

title: PostgreSQL
text: PostgreSQL is a free and open-source relational database management system. It grew out of the Postgres project led by Michael Stonebraker at the University of California, Berkeley, and it supports extensions such as PostGIS for geographic data.

title: Python (programming language)
text: Python is a high-level programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It was developed at Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica in the Netherlands, and the Python Software Foundation now manages its development.

title: Apollo 11
text: Apollo 11 was the spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon, in July 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility while Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit aboard Columbia.

title: French Revolution
text: The French Revolution was a period of political upheaval in France that began in 1789 with the Estates General and the storming of the Bastille in Paris. It ended the monarchy of Louis XVI and led eventually to the rise of Napoleon Bonaparte.

title: Renaissance
text: The Renaissance was a period of European cultural history that began in Florence in the fourteenth century. Artists such as Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo worked during it, supported by patrons such as the Medici family, and it spread across Italy and Europe.

title: Industrial Revolution
text: The Industrial Revolution was the transition to new manufacturing processes that began in Great Britain in the eighteenth century. Mechanized textile production in Manchester, steam power and the growth of railways spread from there to Belgium, Germany and the United States.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
text: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian painter, engineer and scientist of the Renaissance, born in Vinci near Florence. His paintings include the Mona Lisa, which hangs in the Louvre in Paris, and The Last Supper in Milan.

title: Ludwig van Beethoven
text: Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer and pianist born in Bonn who spent most of his career in Vienna. He continued to compose after losing his hearing, and his Ninth Symphony includes a choral setting of Ode to Joy by Friedrich Schiller.

title: William Shakespeare
text: William Shakespeare was an English playwright and poet from Stratford-upon-Avon. His plays, including Hamlet, Macbeth and Romeo and Juliet, were performed by the Lord Chamberlain's Men, many of them at the Globe Theatre in London.

title: Frida Kahlo
text: Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter known for her self-portraits and for works inspired by the culture of Mexico. She lived in Coyoacan in Mexico City, in the house now called the Blue House, and was married to the muralist Diego Rivera.

title: Nobel Prize
text: The Nobel Prizes are international awards established by the will of Alfred Nobel, the Swedish inventor of dynamite. They have been awarded since 1901 for physics, chemistry, medicine, literature and peace, and the Peace Prize is presented in Oslo, Norway.

title: Higgs boson
text: The Higgs boson is an elementary particle in the Standard Model of particle physics, predicted by Peter Higgs and others in 1964. Its discovery at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN was announced in 2012, and Peter Higgs and Francois Englert received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2013.

title: Hubble Space Telescope
text: The Hubble Space Telescope is a space telescope launched into low Earth orbit by the Space Shuttle Discovery in 1990. It is named after the astronomer Edwin Hubble and is operated by NASA with the European Space Agency, with science operations run from Baltimore.
